pages.content:
Services

Stage, lighting, sound and show-calling for corporate gatherings, built from the empty hall up.

Work

We provide complete stage, technical, and live event production for corporate gatherings across four core formats. Every project includes dedicated producer leadership, complete technical direction, and precision stage management from initial brief through load-out.

( 01 )

Kick-offs

Up to 1,600 seated

( 02 )

Award nights

Up to 600 guests

( 03 )

Launches

Up to 250 + stream

( 04 )

Conferences

Plenary and breakouts

( — )

( 01 )

Sales Kick-offs

Our sales kick-off production creates the momentum leadership teams require when addressing commercial organizations. We design staging environments that support executive keynotes, panel discussions, and multi-screen visual presentations for rooms seating up to 1,600 guests. Deliverables include primary stage construction, balanced audio reinforcement for speech, camera packages for audience relays, custom lighting states, and detailed presenter cueing. Every session is timed to the minute, giving commercial directors a controlled platform to align regional teams, announce targets, and maintain continuous audience engagement across multi-day conference schedules without technical hesitation.

( 02 )

Award Nights

Award ceremonies demand absolute acoustic clarity, precise lighting transitions, and flawless stage timing. We engineer the evening to honour recipients with dignity while keeping the ceremony brisk and compelling. Deliverables include walk-up lighting cues, coordinated winner stings, lectern audio systems, stage management with dedicated prompt desks, backstage holding areas, and teleprompter infrastructure for presenters. Priya Raman directs our award productions, coordinating envelope handlers, trophy runners, and audio desks so every category moves forward without dead air, late musical entries, or awkward pauses between nominations and acceptance speeches.

( 03 )

Product Launches

A product reveal leaves no margin for second takes. We build dramatic focus around the unveiling moment through synchronised lighting design, high-definition video playback, and immaculate physical reveals. Deliverables encompass mechanical reveal rigging, custom plinth lighting, redundant media servers, live broadcast audio feeds, and multi-camera live-streaming setups for hybrid audiences. Technical director Ines Duarte oversees the hardware backbone, while Tomasz Okafor calls exact cue sequences to ensure the transition from executive buildup to product exposure happens with theatrical impact and rock-solid broadcast reliability.

( 04 )

Conferences and Off-sites

Corporate conferences and leadership off-sites require consistent technical stewardship across plenary halls and parallel breakout rooms. We handle complete technical infrastructure so company organizers can concentrate entirely on their delegates and agenda. Deliverables include acoustic speech reinforcement, distributed display monitors, presenter comfort monitors, wireless microphone management across adjacent spaces, presentation slide networking, and silent technician dispatch. We establish orderly signal paths, eliminating wireless frequency clashes and presentation delays to deliver an uninterrupted working environment across full multi-day itineraries.

( 01 )

Northline Logistics Annual Kick-off

For Northline Logistics in 2025, Moyooshi Productions designed and staged an annual kick-off gathering for 900 guests. The brief required transforming a large exhibition hall into an intimate plenary environment with crystal-clear sightlines and vocal clarity for executive speakers. We installed a black truss grid, flown line-array audio clusters, and twin projection surfaces flanking a minimal central presentation plinth. Stage manager Tomasz Okafor ran cue transitions across the schedule, keeping the day running on time from the 06:00 load-in through to the final general session.

( 02 )

Halden Engineering Awards Night

In 2026, Halden Engineering engaged us to produce their annual excellence gala for 420 guests. The challenge was maintaining dignity and warmth in an expansive industrial space while executing award presentations with disciplined timing. Producer Priya Raman structured the ceremony run sheet, while lighting designer Kenji Arata programmed warm architectural states and focused lectern spotlights. With prompt monitors, envelope runners, and synchronized audio stings, the evening moved with crisp theatrical rhythm, concluding on time before dinner service without a single missed walk-up cue.

( 03 )

Vesta Audio Product Launch

Vesta Audio required an immaculate live reveal and global webcast in 2026 for 250 in-person industry guests and an international digital audience. Technical director Ines Duarte specified a low-noise lighting rig and uncompressed audio relay to preserve acoustic subtleties during live demonstrations. Our crew installed automated drapery tracking that dropped away on cue, revealing the flagship hardware under sharp sculptural illumination. The hybrid broadcast operated without latency discrepancies between the hall sound and the live stream feed, delivering an uncompromising brand experience to both room guests and remote viewers.

( 04 )

Corporate Conference and Off-site Production Archive

Beyond single-evening galas and product unveilings, our team coordinates intensive multi-day conference and leadership off-site environments. Managing up to 1,600 delegates in flexible hall configurations requires disciplined stage rotations, redundant networking, and immediate technician support across plenary and breakout areas. Lucas Weber manages the logistical load-in and strike sequences, ensuring freight cases, truss components, and cabling leave the venue spotless within hours of final adjournments. Across 214 successful productions since 2014, our standardized documentation and rehearsal protocols ensure that complex executive agendas proceed without technical interruptions.

pages.title: Process
pages.content:
Process

From a first brief to a clean hall, in about six weeks.

Fees

Our delivery process spans a typical brief-to-show duration of six weeks, translating initial executive objectives into a secure, rehearsed production. Every phase is governed by clear milestones, fixed cost frameworks, and precise cue documentation.

( SIX WEEKS )

Six weeks from brief to show.

Every phase has a named owner, a fixed milestone and a printed page. Nothing on show day is a surprise.

( 01 )

The Five-Phase Delivery Framework

We execute every engagement through five disciplined phases. Week 0 is Brief, where client lead Amara Osei and founder Mara Lindqvist review schedule requirements, room capacities, and executive targets. Weeks 1 to 2 encompass Concept and Budget, establishing CAD drawings, technical allocations, and binding line-item figures. Weeks 3 to 5 cover Build and Rehearse, assembling flight cases, verifying line checks, and running cue tests. The fourth phase is Show Day, coordinated through our timed run sheet. The final phase is Strike and Report within five days, providing logistical sign-off, equipment load-out, and financial closure.

( 01 )

Brief

Week 0

You send a brief. We reply within two working days with a first schedule and a rough budget.

( 02 )

Concept and budget

Weeks 1–2

A half-day discovery workshop, then one page with scope, plan and price.

( 03 )

Build and rehearse

Weeks 3–5

Drawings, line checks and a rehearsal against the real cues.

( 04 )

Show day

Load-in 06:00, doors 18:30

The same printed run sheet every time. A named person for each line.

( 05 )

Strike and report

Plus five days

Overnight strike, hall handed back as found, then a written report.

( RUN SHEET )

Day-of-Show Run Sheet

On show days, our 38 on-call crew members follow an exact six-milestone operational schedule. At 06:00 Load-in begins, rolling flight cases into the hall and hoisting primary lighting truss grids. At 10:00 Line check commences, verifying sound levels, optical signals, and redundant video feeds. Rehearsal starts at 14:00, conducting full speaker walk-throughs and cue timing under stage manager Tomasz Okafor. Doors open at 18:30 for guest entry. The Show runs from 19:00 under constant prompt desk supervision. Strike begins at 23:30, dismantling truss and clearing the hall before dawn.

06:00

Load-in

Flight cases roll in, the truss goes up on its hoists.

10:00

Line check

Sound, video and the stream are proved on every path.

14:00

Rehearsal

Every speaker walks the stage against the real cues.

18:30

Doors

Guests arrive into a hall that has already been proved.

19:00

Show

The stage manager calls every cue from the prompt desk.

23:30

Strike

The rig comes down and the hall is handed back by dawn.

( 01 )

Production Price Ledger and Inclusions

Our binding price structure covers six primary production tiers. The Discovery brief workshop is fixed at €1,800. A Half-day kick-off for up to 300 guests starts from €18,000, while a Full-day kick-off starts from €32,000. An Award night hosting up to 600 guests starts from €45,000. A Product launch show starts from €38,000, and Technical production only is billed at €6,500 per day. All figures are stated in euros excluding value-added tax. Each package includes dedicated producer direction from Mara Lindqvist or Priya Raman, technical supervision by Ines Duarte, full sound and lighting rigs, stage management, prompt desk operation, and complete load-in and strike labor.

( FAQ )

Questions before a brief

Five answers we are asked most often.

( 01 )

Are travel and accommodation expenses included in the baseline fees?

Baseline fees cover all labor, planning, equipment staging, and local transport within the Port Ellery metropolitan district. When an event takes place outside our local zone, travel, freight shipping, per diems, and hotel lodging for the assigned crew are itemized transparently in the initial budget estimate during Weeks 1 and 2. We book standard business-grade travel without markup and provide all supporting receipts during the post-show strike and reporting phase. Clients always review and sign off on travel expenditures prior to confirmation.

( 02 )

How do you handle production changes requested during rehearsal?

Stage rehearsals scheduled at 14:00 exist specifically to identify and resolve timing issues or script modifications before doors open at 18:30. Stage manager Tomasz Okafor notes speaker adjustments on the master run sheet immediately and transmits updates to lighting, audio, and video operators in real time. If a client requests substantial hardware additions during rehearsal, technical director Ines Duarte evaluates technical feasibility and confirms safety parameters before client lead Amara Osei presents an exact line-item amendment for executive approval, ensuring no unexpected billing appears on the final account.

( 03 )

Can Moyooshi integrate with existing in-house venue technology?

Yes. While we maintain complete sound, truss, and illumination packages in our Port Ellery warehouse, we regularly interface with installed venue systems to maximize budget efficiency. When booking partner auditoriums, Ines Duarte conducts an initial technical survey during Weeks 1 and 2 to evaluate audio line arrays, tie-lines, and power distribution boards. We then supply the exact front-of-house consoles, microphones, prompt desks, and processing units required to bridge any technical gaps, establishing seamless operation while avoiding duplicate equipment rental charges.

( 04 )

What is your typical briefing lead time and reservation schedule?

Our standard production cycle operates across six weeks from signed discovery brief to show night. This window allows our engineering crew to draft precise CAD layouts, program customized lighting states, secure specialized equipment, and coordinate rehearsal sessions with your executive speakers. For urgent requirements or compressed timelines, client lead Amara Osei reviews crew availability across our 38 on-call specialists to confirm whether safe delivery standards can be maintained before accepting the engagement.

( 05 )

How are invoice payments and cancellation terms structured?

Invoicing follows milestone progress across our five-phase project workflow. An initial commitment deposit is invoiced upon completion of the discovery brief workshop at the start of Week 1. A second milestone payment is due upon completion of the build and rehearsal sign-off in Week 5. The remaining balance is billed following strike and final reporting within five days after the event. Cancellations requested prior to Week 3 forfeit the initial deposit, while cancellations during final build require settling all incurred labor and rental commitments.

About

A production studio in Port Ellery, founded in 2014 by Mara Lindqvist.

Contact

Founded in 2014 in Port Ellery, Moyooshi Productions constructs calm, disciplined live production environments for complex corporate gatherings. We combine engineering precision with clear human leadership to deliver seamless event experiences across Europe and beyond.

( 01 )

Our Trajectory Since 2014

Moyooshi Productions was established in 2014 by executive producer Mara Lindqvist to solve a persistent vulnerability in live events: the absence of disciplined engineering methodology. Operating from our central studio and warehouse at Unit 4, Harbour Works, 18 Quay Road in Port Ellery, we have produced 214 major events since 2014. Our philosophy remains rooted in preparation. We believe the success of any production is secured long before guests arrive, through comprehensive CAD planning, acoustic modelling, and rigorous technical rehearsals. Today, our 38 on-call crew members manage productions ranging from focused 250-seat product launches to 1,600-capacity auditorium conferences, always adhering to our six-week brief-to-show operational discipline.

( 02 )

The Four Crew Desks

Our operational structure is organized across four specialized desks to maintain accountability across every project phase. The Production desk, guided by founder Mara Lindqvist and awards producer Priya Raman, controls scheduling, supplier contracts, and client integration. The Technical desk, led by technical director Ines Duarte and lighting designer Kenji Arata, oversees system engineering, structural truss safety, and audio-visual routing. The Stage desk, directed by stage manager Tomasz Okafor, commands the rehearsal floor, speaker readiness, and live prompt execution. The Logistics desk, managed by Lucas Weber, coordinates trucking, load-in shifts, and complete overnight site strike.

pages.title: Venues & Partners
pages.content:
Venues & Partners

Five kinds of hall we know well, and what each one holds.

Contact

We collaborate with five distinctive architectural hall types across the region to house bespoke corporate productions. Every space is evaluated for rigging load ratings, power distribution, acoustic response, and rapid freight access.

( THE HALL )

Every hall is surveyed before a case is opened.

Rigging points, power and freight access are checked in the concept phase, long before the 06:00 load-in.

( 01 )

Clear-span exhibition hall

Global kick-offs and industry plenaries.

Up to 1,600

( 02 )

Dockland warehouse

Exposed steel and concrete for brand presentations.

Up to 900

( 03 )

Tiered black box

Built-in acoustic baffles for formal ceremonies.

Up to 600

( 04 )

Conference hall

With dedicated breakout spaces.

Up to 420

( 05 )

Daylight studio

Focused product reveals and media demonstrations.

Up to 250

( 01 )

Partner Hall Specifications and Capacities

Our production infrastructure adapts to five primary architectural spaces. Clear-span exhibition halls offer maximum versatility, accommodating our largest configurations of up to 1,600 seated attendees for global kick-offs and industry plenaries. Industrial dockland warehouses accommodate up to 900 guests, offering atmospheric exposed steel and concrete finishes suited for dynamic brand presentations. Tiered black box auditoriums house up to 600 guests with built-in acoustic baffles ideal for formal ceremonies. Contemporary conference halls accommodate up to 420 attendees with dedicated breakout spaces. Daylight studio spaces host focused product reveals and media demonstrations for up to 250 guests.

( 02 )

Technical Venue Survey and Rigging Protocols

Before installing equipment in any partner venue, technical director Ines Duarte conducts an exhaustive on-site audit during the Concept phase. We map high-voltage power distribution boxes, verify certified hanging points for black truss grids, and analyze natural room acoustics to prevent unwanted reverberation. Lucas Weber oversees site logistics, coordinating dock loading bays, freight elevators, and floor protection so that 06:00 load-in proceeds without congestion. Following the event, our crew conducts an extensive venue inspection, returning the hall in spotless condition and documenting load-out sign-off with the local facility director.

posts.title: What a Cue Sheet Is For
posts.excerpt: A production cue sheet is not merely a schedule of speeches, but the binding operational contract that transforms live event uncertainty into calm, synchronized stage execution.
posts.content:
In live event production, panic is rarely caused by faulty equipment. It is caused by ambiguity. When technicians, camera operators, lighting engineers, and executive handlers share an exhibition hall, everyone needs to know exactly what happens next, who initiates it, and when it must occur. This is what a cue sheet is for. Far from being a simple agenda or speaking schedule, a true cue sheet is an operational contract. It translates hours of creative intent and technical calibration into a single, chronological ledger that governs every second of a live show.

At Moyooshi Productions, our cue sheets are built through an exacting method refined across 214 productions since 2014. During the six-week preparation window between initial brief and show day, our four desks—Production, Technical, Stage, and Logistics—contribute directly to its development. The document establishes the key operational criteria for every single transition: the trigger, the caller, the action, and the recovery state. If an executive walks toward a lectern, the cue sheet does not merely say "speaker enters." It specifies the exact spoken word or visual movement that prompts stage manager Tomasz Okafor to call the cue, the radio channel he speaks across, the precise lighting preset Kenji Arata triggers, and the exact fader movement Ines Duarte initiates at the audio console.

This level of precision is tested and finalized during the 14:00 rehearsal milestone on show day. Following the 06:00 load-in and 10:00 line checks, rehearsal provides the single opportunity to run the cue sheet in real time with presenters. Here, pencil marks replace digital drafts. If a presenter delivers a punchline faster than anticipated, or pauses before introducing an award recipient, Tomasz Okafor adjusts the cue line directly on the master document. The prompt desk becomes the absolute source of truth for the entire hall. When doors open at 18:30, our 38 on-call crew members are aligned to the identical sequence, eliminating hesitation and backstage guesswork.

The real power of a disciplined cue sheet reveals itself during moments of deviation. Live events inevitably produce unexpected occurrences: a remote video caller loses audio, a presenter skips two slides, or an award winner walks up the wrong aisle. Without a cue sheet, crew members attempt to guess the producer's intention, resulting in jarring audio cuts or spotlights searching across an empty stage. With a rigorous cue sheet, the stage manager can hold, skip, or modify cues systematically. The crew remains composed because deviations are handled as controlled technical branches rather than operational emergencies.

Ultimately, the cue sheet serves the audience and the client by rendering production invisible. When lighting states shift imperceptibly, microphones open at the exact breath of a speaker, and presentation graphics snap cleanly to video walls, the audience experiences complete immersion in the message. They never see the flight cases, the radio headsets, or the prompt desks. That calm authority is not accidental. It is the direct result of a master cue sheet, drafted with technical discipline and executed with unwavering focus from the first load-in box at 06:00 to the final strike call at 23:30.

posts.title: Vesta Audio product launch
posts.excerpt: Staging an intimate hardware reveal with synchronized lighting and broadcast audio feeds.
posts.content:
Vesta Audio asked for a reveal that felt close: 250 guests in the room, a live stream for press, and a product that had to stay under a cloth until the exact second it was lit. The brief came in six weeks before the date and was answered within two working days.

We built the stage in the warehouse first. The plinth, the lift and the lighting plot were pre-rigged and cabled there, then loaded out in flight cases that rolled straight into the hall at 06:00. Ines Duarte ran the line check at 10:00 and the full technical run-through at 14:00, so the presenter rehearsed against the real cues.

At 19:00 the cloth came off on a single cue called by Tomasz, the light came up on the plinth and the stream feed switched at the same moment. By 23:30 the hall was struck and handed back swept. The debrief report reached Vesta five days later.

posts.title: Halden Engineering awards night
posts.excerpt: Managing 420 seated guests, custom stage lecterns and rapid award pacing.
posts.content:
Halden Engineering recognises its people once a year, in categories that range from site safety to apprenticeship of the year. The night had to feel unhurried for the winners and still finish on time for the four hundred and twenty people at the tables.

Priya Raman wrote the run sheet around the pauses: the walk to the stage, the handshake, the photograph. Each category got a fixed slot and a fixed light state, and Kenji Arata programmed the plot so that the room changed colour only twice. Nothing was improvised after the 14:00 rehearsal.

Doors opened at 18:30, the show started at 19:00 and the last award was presented eight minutes ahead of the sheet. The strike crew led by Lucas Weber had the room cleared before midnight.

posts.title: Northline Logistics annual kick-off
posts.excerpt: Seated plenary staging, wide projection and live show calling for 900 guests.
posts.content:
Northline Logistics brings nine hundred people into one hall for a single morning each year. The brief was short: one stage, one screen, everyone able to see and hear, and nothing on the programme that could run over.

Our crew started load-in at 06:00 with the truss and the projection wall, and the first line check was clear by 10:00. A plain stage and a wide screen kept the room calm; the show caller Tomasz Okafor held the plenary to the minute.

The programme ended on time and the hall was empty again before dusk. The report we sent afterwards listed every cue, every change and every item that went back into the cases.
